answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, with voting weight assigned according to reachable, independently trusted attestations. If wharf, pearl, and meadow are sybil identities concentrated in one cluster, their few edges to honest nodes form a sparse external cut with low conductance. Thus only limited probability mass crosses into the cluster within the walk bound, mathematically limiting its aggregate voting weight regardless of how many identities it creates.
